newsitem.title: BELARUS: Moscow ally Belarus supports NATO treaty.
newsitem.headline: Moscow ally Belarus supports NATO treaty.

text.p: Belarussian President Alexander Lukashenko said on Wednesday he would support the treaty signed on Tuesday between Russia and NATO.
Lukashenko said he had not yet had time to read the text of the NATO-Russia Founding Act in detail.

But the Belarussian leader, who signed a union treaty with Russia last week, said Minsk, like Moscow, continued to oppose NATO plans to admit ex-communist states in eastern Europe although he had to accept the inevitable.
"The interests of Belarus were presented one way or another in the negotiations with NATO," Lukashenko told a news conference.
"Neither Russia nor, still less, Belarus, has a right of veto (over NATO expansion). We have to resign ourselves to reality."
Of the treaty, Lukashenko said: "I'm not going to shout, 'Hooray, we support it'. Yet from what I've heard from Boris Yeltsin, I support this agreement."
The treaty had not reduced the "strategic significance of Belarus", he added.

Minsk, whose union with Moscow leaves both as sovereign states, gave its Soviet-era nuclear missiles to Russia. But its defence contribution to the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), grouping ex-Soviet republics, would remain important, Lukashenko said.

"The significance of the Belarussian air defence cordon is very great and will remain so for the foreseeable future," Lukashenko said. "It's not a trump card, but we do control the entire territory of the CIS."

Lukashenko, whose authoritarian tactics toward the opposition have earned criticism from the West, has said he wants to conclude his own treaty with NATO, which he once referred to as a "dreadful monster".
Minsk also said this month that it wanted to participate in NATO's Partnership for Peace programme after years of boycotting it, despite having formal membership.
